channel.title: Doc Radar
channel.description: Upcoming documentary releases from the distributors, broadcasters, streamers and sales agents that matter. Updated weekly.

item.title: Sam and Colby: Paranormal Investigators (Netflix)
item.description: Best friends Sam and Colby visit some of the world’s most haunted locations in search of paranormal evidence, trying to answer one question: Are ghosts real?

item.title: The Last First: Winter K2 (Apple Original Films)
item.description: Directed by Amir Bar-Lev. A historic race to become the first to summit K2 in winter unravels into tragedy, exposing how ambition, ego, and the pursuit of glory can be as dangerous as the mountain itself.

item.title: Africa Earth's Wild Home
item.description: African wildlife and landscapes is brought to the screen like never before, using the latest technology to tell the most extraordinary stories from the continent and cutting-edge CGI to unearth the deep history and forces that shaped Africa's natural worlds.

item.title: Try!
item.description: Directed by Oisín Mistéil. Four Irish Rugby teams who defy stereotypes tackle their way to the Mixed Ability Rugby World Cup, where full-contact sport meets joyful belonging.

item.title: Kikuyu Land
item.description: Directed by Andrew H. Brown. As a Nairobi journalist probes a land battle entangling the local government and a powerful multinational corporation, covered wounds are revealed and family secrets are exposed.

item.title: Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
item.description: Directed by Alex Gibney. In 2022, Salman Rushdie was preparing to deliver a lecture on the United States as a safe haven for writers when a man rushed the stage and, in 27 seconds, stabbed him 15 times. Airlifted to hospital, Rushdie survived, barely, and his wife Rachel Eliza Griffiths began filming immediately, capturing an unfiltered view of his recovery, return to life and how he regained his spirit and hope for the future.

item.title: Inside the mind of Karl Ove Knausgård
item.description: Directed by Ben Falk. BBC Documentary about the most famous Norwegian writer, Karl Ove Knausgård, author of My Struggle.

item.title: Woven Ground
item.description: Directed by Blair Coron. Composer Blair Coron takes his musical instruments, recording equipment and friends to the islands, glens and forests of Scotland to record directly in the landscapes that inspired the music.

item.title: Hide and Seek
item.description: Directed by Baysalt Gui. This documentary follows two long-lost Ukrainian friends, Arsalan and Nastya, as they reconnect in Germany after russia's full-scale invasion against Ukraine. Arsalan, an actor now in Frankfurt after time in a refugee camp, and Nastya, journalist and producer who stayed in Kyiv, reflect on the divergent paths their lives have taken due to the war. Through their conversations and therapy sessions, the film explores themes of displacement, identity, and the emotional impact of war on youth.

item.title: Secrets of the Southwest: Science Behind the Secrets
item.description: Meet the inspiring individuals and communities who work to protect our most beloved UK wildlife.

item.title: Secrets of the Southwest
item.description: Discover the hidden stories Britain's southwest has to offer. From Foxes fighting on the streets of Bristol to Puffins looking for love on Skomer Island.

item.title: Schumacher ’94 – The Birth of a Legend (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Christin Freitag. Michael Schumacher's first World Championship win roars to life through personal interviews and archival footage of the legendary 1994 Formula 1 season.

item.title: Garden Sanctuary
item.description: Directed by FMDS. My Walk on the 2nd of October.

item.title: Travel Reminiscence
item.description: Directed by Barney Gibbons. At a London community centre, facilitators and volunteers run a travel-themed session for people living with dementia and their families, friends and carers. Together, the group embarks on a playful journey: discussing past trips, revisiting these through theatre, and writing postcards to loved ones.

item.title: Damilola Taylor: The Untold Story
item.description: Directed by Alex Thomas. Ten-year-old Damilola Taylor was fatally stabbed in 2000 in a stairwell in Peckham, South East London, just metres from his home. 'Star Wars' star John Boyega, who also grew up in Peckham, speaks for the first time about being one of the last people to see him alive, sharing the fear and uncertainty that followed in the aftermath of Taylor's death. Boyega is joined by close friends and family members of Taylor, who reveal the events that led to his death and talk for the first time about the impact his tragic murder has had in shaping their lives.

item.title: Karl
item.description: Directed by Nick Hooker. “I have spent so much time playing a role that it’s almost impossible for anyone to know who I really am,” Karl Lagerfeld once proclaimed. The German fashion designer, creative director and cultural force, who dominated the world of fashion for more than seven decades, is finally revealed in ravishing detail.

item.title: The Dance of the Kokorrdit
item.description: Directed by Elio B Cunampio. A Wounaan teenager and a leader of their community venture into the Darién in search of a sacred bird. Along the way, they will face the dangers that threaten their territory and their culture.

item.title: Kibboutz Nir Oz, aux portes de Gaza (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Olga Kravets.

item.title: The Fight to Be Heard
item.description: Directed by Leah Rustomjee. The Amnesty International UK explores the human stories behind protest and the growing pressures faced by protesters in the UK today.

item.title: Mafia: Behind the Bloodshed
item.description: Directed by Max Serio. Mafia: Behind the Bloodshed reveals the real-world operations, structures, and history of major global organized crime groups.

item.title: Who Is Martin Mull? (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Neil Berkeley. Discover Martin Mull's restless reinvention from smoky folk clubs to primetime sitcoms to gallery walls, told in his own words and by the friends who watched it happen, including Steve Martin, Tom Waits, David Alan Grier and others.

item.title: The Serial Killer Connection
item.description: The series investigates serial killer Richard “Marc” Evonitz, who kidnapped, assaulted, and murdered multiple young girls (including Sofia Marlene Silva, Kristin Michelle Lisk, and Kathryn Nicole Lisk

item.title: The World Came Flooding In
item.description: Directed by Isobel Knowles. The World Came Flooding In is an immersive VR documentary reconstructing memories of the eastern Australia floods in 2022, which is representative of similar events that happened recently in various parts of the world.

item.title: Landscapes of Shame
item.description: Directed by Patrick Hough. Navigating Ireland’s haunted landscapes, ecological extinction and cultural suppression emerge as intertwined forms of colonial erasure.

item.title: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger
item.description: Directed by Dylan Southern. Experience the meteoric rise of Oasis through rare footage and untold stories as the band reunites for Oasis Live '25, chronicling their journey from Manchester streets to global rock stardom.

item.title: The Disciple: A Wu-Tang Fable (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Joanna Natasegara. This documentary recounts Cilvaringz's unlikely rise from fan to Wu-Tang Clan fame — and how the infamous "Once Upon a Time in Shaolin" album came to be.

item.title: Lesbian Lines
item.description: Directed by Cara Holmes. In a silenced Ireland, a community of lesbians builds an underground network of helplines - offering connection, survival, and defiance through the simple act of answering the phone.

item.title: André Leon Talley — Style is Forever (Greenwich Entertainment)
item.description: Directed by Zach Stafford. André Leon Talley was a trailblazing fashion icon whose influence spanned nearly five decades. This documentary explores his legacy of inclusivity, elegance, and the fearless pursuit of authenticity. Interviews with Anna Wintour, Tom Ford and Diane von Furstenberg, among others, as well as never-before-seen footage, reveal Talley’s personal and professional challenges and remarkable triumphs.

item.title: The Sound We Make Together
item.description: Directed by Maddalena Cagol. Striving for fame, is that the right reason to be head over heels in the competitive music industry? It's no secret that the music industry is one of the toughest out there…creative slumps, isolation, the fear of 'not making it' and failure. So, we introduce The Hills Brothers, a brotherly duo of musicians, local to Portsmouth, who spend their nights hosting several Open Mic nights all over Portsmouth and Hampshire. Take a deeper look into why they find these Open Mic nights more than just a fun night to express yourself and your music. Understand why these nights create a community for musicians and why venues like Casemates are essential for the artists support.

item.title: Mucker
item.description: Directed by Titus Fossgard-Moser. Mucker provides a fascinating insight into the professional and personal life of the pioneering and award winning British documentary film maker Brian Moser.

item.title: Le grand jeu de Jessica Chastain (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Patrick Boudet.

item.title: The Great Maia
item.description: Directed by David James Armsby. "Great Maia" is an extra-special film of the "Dinosauria Animated Series", it is set in the Two Medicine Formation during the Late Cretaceous and follows a young first-time mother Maiasaura as she tries to protect her first clutch of eggs.

item.title: Dreamscape
item.description: Directed by Meray Diner. Dreamscape is a quest on the weight of times we never imagined would become our reality. In the quiet hours of sleep, when our defenses soften, buried emotions rise to the surface, often more vivid than waking life. For those shaped by migration and marked by generational trauma, dreams become both a refuge and a mirror. This film explores how the unconscious mind reflects collective and personal struggle. It journeys through the inner worlds we create to survive, to heal, and to simply endure whether that's building coping mechanisms through faith, art, somatics or activism.

item.title: The Pet Cemetery Murders: A Ghost Story (HBO Documentary Films)
item.description: The re-opening of a mysterious 1985 cold case murder in Louisiana unearths a haunting history of bloodshed and long-buried trauma.

item.title: Cosmic Symphony
item.description: Directed by Laura Karpman. Four iconic instruments, including The Wizard of Oz and A Star Is Born pianos, all lost in the 2025 Los Angeles Fires, are celebrated by their musicians, culminating in an animated send-off towards an imagined future, a Cosmic Symphony. Directed by Oscar-nominated composer Laura Karpman, and featuring John Clayton, Susie Chung, Starr Parodi and Diane Warren, Cosmic Symphony explores a truth that every musician knows - musical instruments have souls.

item.title: The Fall and Rise of the Barras
item.description: Directed by Gavin Lundy. Director Gavin Lundy explores the resurgence of Glasgow's famous Barras Market only to find new questions of identity in a changing city.

item.title: Always Lalisa
item.description: Directed by Sue Kim. Documentary following global superstar LISA during a transformative year away from BLACKPINK, the K-pop phenomenon that made her one of the world's most recognizable performers. Documenting a year of risk, reinvention, and self-discovery as LISA begins to define her next chapter.

item.title: Free Leonard Peltier (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Jesse Short Bull. Leonard Peltier, one of the surviving leaders of the American Indian Movement, has been in prison for 50 years following a contentious conviction. A new generation of Native activists is committed to winning his freedom before he dies.

item.title: Transformation
item.description: Directed by Ganna Tretiak. A feature-length documentary exploring the profound inner metamorphosis of Ukrainian civilians from the creative sector who chose to enlist as soldiers to defend their country. The film maps the deep psychological and lifestyle shifts experienced by musicians, artists, and filmmakers as they stepped away from civilian art to enter the realities of war.

item.title: A Norway Visit : Skjolden
item.description: Directed by Alfie Bristow. Skjolden is a beautiful and luscious town in Norway's deepest and longest fjord of Sognefjord. Camouflaged in the bright, green mountains lies tips, facts and awe which will capture any viewer's attention.

item.title: Me, Myself and Vegas
item.description: Directed by Tyler-James. A young woman from England struggling to find a partner to walk her down the aisle goes to Las Vegas where she marries herself in this documentary of self love.

item.title: Ask E. Jean (BBC Storyville)
item.description: The thrilling story of E. Jean Carroll’s life, from her early days as Miss Cheerleader USA to her rise as a trailblazing journalist, author, and beloved advice columnist. Carroll broke barriers as the first female editor at Esquire, Playboy, and Outside, helping to redefine women’s roles in media with her sharp wit and fearless voice. In recent years, she reignited public discourse by standing up to power, becoming the only woman to beat Donald Trump twice in court, and sparking a national conversation about truth, accountability, and resilience. A portrait of an indomitable woman who proved it’s never too late to reclaim your voice, rewrite your story, and change the world.

item.title: TYSON (Netflix)
item.description: Explore the explosive life of Mike Tyson — one of the most feared and fascinating figures in sports history.

item.title: The Search for Leah Croucher: A Parent's Nightmare
item.description: Directed by Jonathan Drake. A two-part document about the disappearance of a 19-year-old woman in the English town of Milton Keynes in 2019.

item.title: We Are Made of Star Stuff (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Nanette Burstein. An intimate and cinematic portrait of astronomer and planetary scientist Carl Sagan, we explore his romance with partner Ann Druyan and with science. Featuring exclusive audio recordings, archival clips and animation, along with interviews with his family, friends and colleagues. With the full support of Sagan’s family and friends, We Are Made of Star Stuff presents a fascinating look into the life and career of one of the world’s most inspiring and revolutionizing scientists of our time.

item.title: Lady Liberty: Secrets of an Icon (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Julien Johan. This iconic statue was a gift from France to the new-born American Republic and was the first crowd-funded monument of all time. A symbol of emancipation and freedom, which took two decades to be completed. The film features original 3D virtual reconstitutions of Auguste Bartholdi’s Atelier in Paris and travels back in time to bring viewers at the heart of the Statue’s original construction, revealing the founding ideals of our democracies.

item.title: Corregidora: The Darkest Night in Mexican Soccer
item.description: Revisits the events of March 5, 2022, during the match between Querétaro and Atlas, reconstructing what unfolded and examining its aftermath, the conflicting narratives surrounding the case, and the questions that, four years later, remain unresolved.

item.title: NAZA
item.description: Directed by Yuval Abraham. Filmed at night from Tel Aviv rooftops, this investigative documentary examines the civilian casualties of Israel's military operations in Gaza and the systems behind targeted killings of Palestinians.

item.title: Norm: The Tale of Norm Macdonald (Netflix)
item.description: Directed by Judd Apatow. Go down a wormhole in this documentary on master of deadpan humor Norm Macdonald, whose life and career were uncompromising yet full of contradictions.

item.title: Hometown Giants
item.description: Step inside the Vancouver Giants major junior hockey team, where celebrity owners Michael Bublé and Drew Scott set out to revive a franchise that hasn't won a championship since 2007. For the players, they're teenagers living away from home, finishing high school, and chasing NHL dreams they've built their lives around, even though only a few will ever make it.

item.title: Duckweed
item.description: Directed by Matthew Berka. Obscure, aging, and living on the outskirts of London, writer of supernatural fiction Quentin Crisp asks himself a fundamental existential question: ‘Who am I?' This feature-length film-essay is structured around readings of Crisp’s own zuihitsu of the same name, which, in essence, is the story of his life. As we follow Crisp on a walk deeper into the ‘‘little wood’’ of his private landscape, the binaries of success and failure begin to fade away.

item.title: STYMIE
item.description: A documentary based on the word 'stymie'.

item.title: S K 8
item.description: Directed by Alexander Baguley. Four Skaters Skate

item.title: Alex Jones: One Day in Aberfan
item.description: Alex Jones marks the 60th anniversary of the mining disaster that claimed 114 lives, including 116 children

item.title: Aberfan: The Village That Fought Back
item.description: Directed by Ceri Isfryn. Aberfan's grieving community takes on the government, demanding justice and removal of the remaining tips after the disaster that killed 144 people

item.title: Unseen: The Aberfan Portraits
item.description: Following the Aberfan disaster in 1966, an artist from Llandudno embarked on an extraordinary mission to paint portraits of most of the 116 children who lost their lives, using photographs and locks of hair provided by their grieving families. For the first time, relatives share what these remarkable paintings have meant to them over the past six decades. Presented by the BBC’s Huw Thomas, he discovers how the portraits became enduring symbols of remembrance in a village touched by tragedy.

item.title: Enter the Television
item.description: Directed by Thomas Edward Seymour. From Tom Seymour creator of the VHS Massacre Trilogy. Enter the Television is a feature-length documentary exploring the dark corners of television from obscure commercials to unconventional cable programming. It examines the evolution of media through an underground lens, revealing how independent voices survive within systems controlled by powerful media corporations.

item.title: Forza on the Run
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 02: The French police have put the illegal drift racers of Paris on final notice, so they've took off on the run across the border into Belgium. Hanrahan rides along with the crew as they dodge police and takeover Brussels.

item.title: TOMORROW X TOGETHER WORLD TOUR 'ACT : TOMORROW'
item.description: Directed by Yum Tae-hwan. Like shining stars, TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s fourth world tour 'ACT : TOMORROW' unfolds as a dazzling journey toward the tomorrow they promised together. From its beautiful storytelling to the stunning production and powerful live performances that captivated MOA around the world, experience the immersive energy of TOMORROW X TOGETHER’s spectacular world tour on the big screen!

item.title: The Emerald Underground
item.description: Directed by Darren Kelly. A short documentary following the stories of three independent bands from across Ireland; The Psychs, IMLÉ and Dead Assets. Each band shares their passion for music, the many struggles they face on their journey, and what keeps them going.

item.title: SEVENTEEN WORLD TOUR 'NEW_'
item.description: Directed by Yum Tae-hwan. Celebrating their 10th debut anniversary, SEVENTEEN embarks on a world tour fueled by their determination for a fresh start, just like the title 'NEW_'. With their unrivaled stage presence and explosive energy, SEVENTEEN once again proves their unlimited potential. Experience the blazing heat of the concert—bursting with each member’s unique charm—right on the big screen!

item.title: Back to the Beginning: Ozzy's Final Bow
item.description: Directed by Ben Wainwright-Pearce. A powerful return to roots, this concert captures Black Sabbath in peak form - reuniting to deliver classic hits with raw energy and legendary precision.

item.title: Der Schatz von Assisi (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Paolo Colangeli.

item.title: Everest: The Other Side (National Geographic Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Jimmy Chin. An intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible. Elite ski mountaineers Jim Morrison and Hilaree Nelson fell deeply in love while reaching the pinnacle of their sport. Their drive sharpened into a shared dream: to climb and ski the direct North Face of Mount Everest—the most difficult and dangerous climb on the mountain and the most coveted ski line on Earth—something only a handful have ever achieved, and no one has successfully skied down.

item.title: When a Witness Recants (HBO Documentary Films)
item.description: Directed by Dawn Porter. In 1983, author Ta-Nehisi Coates learned that a 14-year-old boy was murdered in his Baltimore middle school. Upon revisiting the case, he uncovers the truth: Three innocent teenagers were wrongfully convicted and spent 36 years in prison — creating a lasting impact on the accused, the witnesses, and their community.

item.title: All About the Money
item.description: Directed by Sinéad O'Shea. A son of one of America’s wealthiest families creates a communist revolutionary base in rural Massachusetts as a means of disrupting the capitalist system he grew up in, but has now come to despise. It’s the starting point of an astonishing journey.

item.title: Occupational Hazard: The First Coral Reefers
item.description: Directed by John H. Cunningham. Journey through the 1970s and early ’80s with the original members of Jimmy Buffett's Coral Reefer Band as they recount their contributions to iconic albums, life on tour, and the lasting impact they had in shaping a unique and enduring genre of music.

item.title: Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down
item.description: Directed by Christoph Farwig. "Don't Let The Bastards Grind You Down" is a documentary film about British social policy. The focus is on the political struggle against neoliberal austerity policies, which have their origins in the hated Thatcher government. The film features the former socialist MP Dave Nellist, who is now the national chair of the Trade Unionist & Socialist Coalition and Hannah Sell, the general secretary of the Socialist Party. The film features a local election campaign in the miners' town of Nuneaton, students campaigning against an increase in tuition fees and refuse workers from Birmingham striking against massive cuts to their wages.

item.title: Beyond
item.description: Directed by Ben Menashe. Beyond follows people living with and beyond cancer as they discover strength, connection, and a new sense of possibility through climbing. Set between indoor walls and wild mountain rock, it is a powerful story about recovery becoming adventure.

item.title: Making Marie Antoinette
item.description: Directed by Eleanor Coppola. Eleanor Coppola's behind-the-scenes documentation of her daughter Sofia Coppola directing the 2006 film Marie Antoinette, capturing the craftsmanship and challenges of being a young female director.

item.title: George Michael: The Faith Tour
item.description: Directed by Andy Morahan. A stunning delve into George Michael's 1988 Faith Tour, as shot live at the famous Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy. This exclusive footage, assembled from a 14-camera shoot captured on 35mm over two nights (30–31 May 1988), features the 24-year-old pop star at the height of his powers.

item.title: Avedon
item.description: Directed by Ron Howard. Richard Avedon’s photographs didn’t just reflect culture, they shaped it, and continue to do so. The feature documentary AVEDON traces the life and legacy of an artist who used fashion, portraiture, and commercial photography to explore identity, power, fear and beauty. With unprecedented access to Avedon’s archive, including never before seen photos, behind the scenes recordings, and interviews with those who knew him best, AVEDON is a visually stunning examination of the mind of an artist who shaped our collective image of the 20th century.

item.title: Finding Faith
item.description: Directed by Mary McCartney. A short film contextualising the cultural significance of George Michael's Faith Tour via unheard interview voice-over, unseen images by Herb Ritts, and behind-the-scenes footage of the Faith music video.

item.title: Whispers in the Woods
item.description: Directed by Vincent Munier. In the heart of the tranquil Vosges forests, where lynxes, bears and deer roam freely, Vincent Munier accompanies his father on his expeditions. He not only seeks to capture the visual wonders of this forest kingdom, but also aims to make its sounds audible. Every whisper of the forest is a reminder of the knowledge of nature that his father once imbued in him – knowledge that Vincent now passes on to his own son. Vincent Munier combines breathtaking footage of nature and its sounds to create a fairytale-like cinematic experience that slows time down.

item.title: Nuisance Bear
item.description: Directed by Gabriela Osio Vanden. A polar bear is forced to navigate a human world of tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as its ancient migration collides with modern life. When a sacred predator is branded a nuisance, it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

item.title: 1 in 2
item.description: Directed by David Wilkinson. Nearly one in two of us will be diagnosed with cancer at some point in our lives. David Nicholas Wilkinson is one of them, twice over. 1 in 2 follows Wilkinson through his own treatment, where he discovers a steep rise in bowel cancer among people far too young to be screened for it, and far too young, it seems, to be believed.

item.title: Whiddy (ARTE)
item.description: Directed by Adrian McCarthy. A small rural community in Ireland welcomes in a major, global oil company with open arms but just 10 years and numerous oil spills later, that dream turns into an unimaginable nightmare. 50 lives lost in a tragedy that silenced and divided the community and still haunts it to this day.

item.title: The Neighbourhood is Changing
item.description: Documentary on the making and legacy of Mulberry Street featuring new interviews with cast and crew

item.title: You Can See Everything
item.description: Directed by Nathan Fielder. Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

item.title: American Doctor
item.description: Directed by Poh Si Teng. United by a shared oath to save lives, three American doctors—Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—work in a besieged hospital in Gaza and return to the United States to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind.

item.title: Phantom 814
item.description: Directed by Jake Hanrahan. Heavy Weekend 03: Unique access to the most mysterious organisation in France. Jake Hanrahan travels with the bizarre syndicate known as "814SSR". They shoot guns, host fight clubs, and make money in the underground. Yet still, they insist they're not a gang and are simply doing hardcore trolling. The truth? Decide for yourself...

item.title: Remember the Summit
item.description: Directed by Timothy Dhalleine. Sir Chris Bonington’s return to Torres del Paine, 62 years after the first ascent of the Central Tower. At 91 years old, and while living with Alzheimer’s disease, the documentary accompanies Bonington in a profoundly human return: an attempt to reconnect with memories that time has erased, but that the Patagonian landscape still seems to guard. During the filming, Chris once again set foot on the territory of Estancia Cerro Guido, closing a circle between past and present, between the epic of mountaineering and the fragility of memory.

item.title: SO ALIVE!
item.description: Directed by yennik arual. A fictional boy aims to become a non-fictional rapper. His label has other plans.

item.title: 14th
item.description: Directed by Ava DuVernay. Revolves around the equal protection and citizenship-focused 14th amendment, which was ratified in 1868 in the turbulent era of Reconstruction and has been a contentious part of the American body politic ever since.

item.title: Rehearsals for a Revolution
item.description: Directed by Pegah Ahangarani. Through five portraits of relatives and mentors, five expressions of resistance, Pegah Ahangarani sketches her life story. Drawing from personal archives, home videos, street protests footage, newspapers, and recorded voices, she retraces more than 40 years of Iran’s history. From the early days of 1979, until the war that began in 2026, she pieces together intimate and collective memories, forming the portrait of a country shaped by political repression and in constant hope for a revolution.

item.title: Each Day in a Moment: 2026
item.description: Directed by Sam O. Burgess. One person’s perspective of the year 2026 shown through an accumulation of 365 unedited shots.

item.title: Renoir & Love
item.description: Directed by Ali Ray. Pierre-Auguste Renoir is one of the world’s favourite artists, a founding member of the Impressionist movement and a constantly evolving artist. With exclusive access to the National Gallery’s new exciting show of the same name (3 October 2026 – 31 January 2027), Exhibition on Screen will bring Renoir’s world class works to cinema audiences. Be transported back to a Parisian summer of love through the eyes of a true visionary. An unmissable opportunity to fall in love with Renoir this winter.
